La Martingale est le podcast de finances: La Martingale is the personal finance podcast launched in 2019 by Matthieu Stefani, also behind Génération Do It Yourself, MediaCritic's previous episode. Alongside him is Sébastien Couasnon, whom we'd met on Tech 45', with Orso Media producing — at this point less a studio than a solar system. The idea: dust off saving and investing. More than 340 episodes later, it covers real estate, forests, bitcoin, collectible watches and private equity.
Le nom, lui, est un cas d'école. Une mar: The name itself is a textbook case. A martingale is the betting strategy where you double your stake after every loss: foolproof on paper, ruinous in practice. Around the podcast orbit a YouTube channel, articles, a fortnightly newsletter and a Discord. Yes, a Discord to talk about life insurance.
Le format historique : Matthieu Stefani: The original format: Matthieu Stefani hosts a specialist from a sector and asks the questions a financial salesperson has no desire to hear. The promise is in black and white: fees, performance, risks.
L'antenne libre du mardi, animée par Ama: The Tuesday open line, hosted by Amaury de Tonquédec: experts answer listeners' questions. The format that convinced us least, with a whiff of a finance call-in radio show.
Des épisodes thématiques pour poser les: Themed episodes to lay the groundwork: "Is your savings asleep?", "ETFs vs active management, the match", "How to invest for retirement".
En France, on parle de son psy, de son d: In France, people talk about their shrink, their divorce, their cold therapy, but not about what they earn, what they've saved, and even less what they've lost. La Martingale takes on that last taboo, from its most boring and most decisive angle: fees. Its real value isn't telling you where to invest, but teaching you to think about your money and to ask the right questions of whoever wants to sell you something. To start, pick a topic that already speaks to you: real estate if you dream of buy-to-let, bitcoin if crypto has always intrigued you.
Trois réserves et demie, pourtant. Le gr: Three and a half reservations, though. The big one: a podcast about investing, funded by investment players, inviting investment players. The awkward questions make up for it without guaranteeing independence: it's an ecosystem outlet, not a consumer outlet. Stefani is an investor himself, which gives him expertise and creates a grey area worth keeping in mind. The audience remains fairly savvy, fairly urban, fairly well-off: investing in a forest doesn't speak to someone ending the month a hundred euros in the red. And the half: the name promises a foolproof system when the whole show explains there isn't one. They contradict themselves from the opening credits, but with elegance.
« Sur trente ans, ce sont les frais qui: “Over thirty years, it's the fees that decide, not your gut.”
